title: U.S. House · New Jersey's 12th District
area: Most of Mercer County (Trenton, Princeton) plus parts of Middlesex and Somerset counties, including Plainfield and parts of Piscataway.

context.text: Incumbent Rep. Bonnie Watson Coleman (D) did not seek re-election and withdrew from the Democratic primary ballot, leaving NJ-12 an open seat for the first time since 2014. Adam Hamawy won a 13-candidate Democratic primary on June 2, 2026 with 28.6% of the vote. Gregg Mele won the Republican primary unopposed. Andres Jinete (Green Party) and Winston Jordan (No Party Affiliation) also qualified for the November 3 general-election ballot.

candidates.name: Adam Hamawy
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary with 28.6% of the vote in a 13-candidate field

summary.text: Adam Hamawy is the Democratic nominee for New Jersey's open 12th Congressional District. A surgeon and U.S. Army veteran, he served as a combat trauma surgeon in Iraq and treated patients at Ground Zero after 9/11. He has since practiced emergency and reconstructive medicine in New Jersey and volunteered on medical missions in conflict and disaster zones, including Gaza in 2024 and 2025.

background.text: Grew up in Old Bridge, New Jersey; earned an ROTC scholarship to attend Rutgers University and Rutgers Medical School (Rutgers University-Newark), also holding a graduate degree from Rutgers University at Camden.
Served in the New Jersey Army National Guard and U.S. Army, rising to the rank of Lieutenant Colonel; served as a combat trauma surgeon in Iraq (2003-2011 period of service).
Treated victims and first responders at a field hospital at Ground Zero on September 11, 2001, during his medical residency.

Built a medical practice in Princeton, New Jersey, and has volunteered treating patients in war and disaster zones over 30 years, including Bosnia, Haiti, Sudan, Colombia, Syria, Lebanon, and Gaza; was present in Gaza during Israel's seizure of the Rafah Crossing in 2024-2025 and said he refused to leave until his colleagues, including U.S. green-card holders, were guaranteed safe passage.
Was Rep. Bonnie Watson Coleman's guest at the 2025 State of the Union address.

priorities.text: Achieving universal healthcare through Medicare for All rather than continued military spending, saying "we have our priorities wrong as a country."
priorities.quote: Healthcare, Not Bombs - We have our priorities wrong as a country. We should be spending our resources on achieving universal healthcare through Medicare for All, not bombs and endless wars.

priorities.text: Abolishing U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), saying immigrant communities are under attack from federal agencies he describes as "out of control."
priorities.quote: Abolish ICE - Our immigrant neighbors are under attack and federal agencies like ICE are out of control. We need to protect our neighbors and restore civil rights in this country.

priorities.text: "Unrigging" the economy so it works for working people rather than what he calls "billionaires at the top."

positions.summary: Supports achieving universal healthcare through Medicare for All.
positions.quote: We should be spending our resources on achieving universal healthcare through Medicare for All, not bombs and endless wars.

positions.summary: Supports abolishing ICE, saying the agency is "out of control" and that immigrant communities need protection.

candidates.name: Gregg Mele
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 2, 2026 Republican primary unopposed

summary.text: Gregg Mele is the Republican nominee for New Jersey's open 12th Congressional District. He holds degrees in law, business, and education, and has worked as an educator. His campaign centers on reducing federal spending and regulation, border security, and support for Israel.

background.text: Earned a bachelor's degree from Montclair State University, graduate degrees from Stevens Institute of Technology, New York University, and CUNY Baruch College, and a law degree from New York Law School.
Career experience includes working as an educator, in law, business, finance, and technology.

priorities.text: Lowering family costs through disciplined federal spending, expanded American energy production, and relief from regulation.
Securing the border and supporting law enforcement to keep communities safe.
Requiring Congress to answer what new spending will cost, how it will be paid for, and whether it will work before approving it.
priorities.quote: Make Congress answer three questions before spending: What will it cost? How will it be paid for? Will it actually work?

positions.summary: Supports securing the border and enforcing immigration law.
Supports law enforcement funding as part of keeping New Jersey communities safe.
Supports standing with Israel and strengthening American leadership abroad.
Says he will "put patients first" by expanding choice and protecting the doctor-patient relationship from what he calls "one-size-fits-all Washington control," rather than expanding public coverage.
Campaign platform calls for defending parental rights and keeping schools focused on academic excellence, framed as part of protecting parents' role in education decisions.

summary.text: Andres Jinete is the Green Party nominee for New Jersey's open 12th Congressional District. A community organizer and member of the Central Jersey Tenant Union and Workers Strike Back, he has worked on tenant advocacy and rapid-response networks opposing ICE detentions, and previously worked in libraries serving the district.

background.text: Community organizer and member of the Central Jersey Tenant Union and Workers Strike Back.
Advocated for tenants and seniors in a large apartment complex in his town, resulting in code violations being addressed.
Helped build rapid-response networks across New Jersey to support working people and small businesses and to prevent ICE detentions in their communities.
Worked for several years at libraries in the district, serving disadvantaged populations and developing programs for seniors and families.

priorities.text: National rent control covering residential and commercial properties, plus large-scale investment in income-based social housing.
priorities.quote: We are fighting for national rent control that includes residential and commercial properties, and for a massive investment in social housing which will provide high-quality, income based units.

priorities.text: Universal, single-payer healthcare and a patent-free drug market.
priorities.quote: The insurance companies and Big Pharma use both the Democrat and Republican parties to hold back single-payer healthcare and a patent-free drug market.

priorities.text: Purchasing and forgiving all outstanding federal student loan debt and reinstating tuition-free public colleges and universities.

positions.summary: Supports national rent control for residential and commercial properties and a major expansion of income-based social housing.
Supports single-payer, universal healthcare and a patent-free drug market.
Has organized rapid-response networks in New Jersey aimed at preventing ICE detentions in communities.

summary.text: Winston Jordan is a No Party Affiliation candidate for New Jersey's open 12th Congressional District, running what he calls a "no money, no donation" campaign that accepts no campaign contributions of any kind. An Army veteran and IT professional, he describes himself as a progressive advocating for a renewal of New Deal-era economic guarantees.

background.text: Born in Brooklyn, New York; served in the U.S. Army from 1976 to 1978 and earned a military citation from Big Bend Community College in 1977.
Career experience includes working as an IT professional and author.

priorities.text: Running a campaign that accepts no donations from individuals, corporations, PACs, unions, or lobbies of any kind.
priorities.quote: I accept absolutely no campaign money of any kind — not small-dollar, not large-dollar, not from individuals, not from corporations, PACs, unions, lobbies, or any entity whatsoever.

priorities.text: Redirecting federal resources directly to residents of NJ-12 rather than corporate beneficiaries of federal policy, including free education and direct investment to eliminate poverty.
Reviving New Deal-era economic guarantees, describing his platform as "FDR2.0" and citing the rights to a useful job, a living wage, adequate medical care, and a decent home.

positions.summary: Cites "the right to adequate medical care and the opportunity to achieve and enjoy good health" among the New Deal-era guarantees he wants restored.

sources.title: United States House of Representatives elections in New Jersey, 2026

researchNotes: Adam Hamawy's and Andres Jinete's positions and priorities are drawn from their Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey answers (their own words); Winston Jordan's from a 2025 survey he completed. Gregg Mele has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey, so his positions are drawn from his campaign website's issue summaries rather than direct Q&A, and his campaign website's dedicated candidate-bio subpage returned a 404 error, so his background is limited to what Ballotpedia and his homepage state. No candidate in this race has held prior elected office, so there is no official voting or bill-sponsorship record to report for any of them.
